title: the worker and the reviewer in a target checkout
acceptance: Implements design.md sections 15.3 and 15.6 for runs. For a non-default project fm-worker.sh runs fm-project.sh sync and verify first and stops on their refusal; creates the worktree at state/projects/<name>/worktrees/<task> from the managed clone at the project's base; pushes the task branch to the project's github repository; opens and looks up the pull request with gh --repo against base. The pull request body carries task id, title, acceptance, scope and the `spec pin: <project>/<task>#<n> <sha256 prefix>` line.

fm-review.sh, fm-checkpoint.sh, fm-cleanup.sh and fm-reconcile.sh take --project and act only in that project's clone, worktree root and repository. fm-cleanup.sh refuses anything that is not a direct child of that project's worktree root (section 5.2a).

Nothing in section 15.6's never-write list reaches the target: .fm-prompt.md and .fm-say.md are excluded locally and never committed, and no push goes to base. Any new worker exit code is added to section 5.3.2's list.
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
